title: Domination of a Gaussian product measure
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in\bbr$, and let $x\in\bbr^n$. Let $v\ge0$ with $v\ne0$, and suppose $v+\rho^2=1$. Then there is a finite nonnegative extended real constant $C$ such that the product of the Gaussian measures with means $\rho x_i$ and variance $v$ is dominated by $C$ times the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is a real vector of length $n$
